chapter: La Rocca on who created jazz
title: Jelly Roll Morton's claim and Milenberg Joys
summary: Rust cites Morton's Library of Congress claims; La Rocca says Morton stole from the ODJB.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: So that the opening words of the late Jelly Roll Morton on his talk for the Library of Congress in Washington, with Alan Lomax, is wrong completely. He says from the very first, the first words he says on those records is, jazz started in New Orleans. And he goes on to tell about how he wrote Tiger Rag, how he named it, and how it was based on the old French quadrilles and all the rest of that stuff. Well, you've told me already, and I believe you absolutely, that that is just so much hooey.
Well, as far as him, he stole his music from the original Dixieland jazz band. You don't have to go any further than that Mellenberg Jaws.
